BrasilAgro's own portfolio appraisal: Deloitte third-party appraisal R$3.5B (vs internal R$3.1B), implying ~R$13,800/hectare = ~R$5,580/acre weighted across 252K hectares

methodology:
BrasilAgro is unusual in having a recent third-party appraisal (Deloitte) of its entire portfolio at R$3.5B — disclosed in the FY2024/25 annual report. The internal valuation is R$3.1B. Both values exceed the GAAP balance-sheet book of R$512.8M (which uses cost rather than fair-value accounting under Brazilian GAAP). The R$3.5B Deloitte mark across 252K hectares implies ~R$13,800/hectare = ~R$5,580/acre weighted.

The Property table aggregates by farm where data is available. Major farms publicly disclosed: Jatobá (Bahia, 31,606 ha grains, acquired 2007), Cremaq (Piauí, grains, 2006), Alto Taquari residual (MT, ~1,300 ha sugarcane after partial sales). Plus international holdings in Paraguay and Bolivia. Other Brazilian farms aggregated into a single line.

Two recent BrasilAgro dispositions provide useful real-world marks:
- Chaparral Farm (Bahia, 37,183 ha grains) sold March 2024 for R$364.5M = ~R$9,800/hectare
- Preferência Farm (Bahia, 17,799 ha) sold June 2025 for R$141.4M = ~R$7,940/hectare with implied 9.3% IRR

All transaction comps are dated within 24 months. Western Bahia (Jatobá) is marked at R$8,500/acre to reflect the LEM region's premium; Cremaq at R$6,500 reflects Matopiba's logistics discount; the "Other" aggregate uses ~R$5,500/acre matching the Deloitte weighted average.

BrasilAgro discloses currency, segments, and farm-level acreage cleaner than most farmland operators. Total FMV vs. book is materially higher because Brazilian GAAP carries land at cost; under the same fair-value model that Australian REITs use, the gap would not exist.
